I, Hasan, expected him to stop visiting the music room after that. Each went alone to the quiet library behind the mosque to ask the keeper of records who was right, and each was sent home with the same answer: come back together. seed.topicSeed: a night bus in Manchester; a captain and a stowaway over how to describe an accident honestly

g.passage: Rain-streaked windows rattled as the night bus pulled away from Piccadilly, and Jonah dropped into the seat beside me as if we had planned it. Three weeks earlier he had hidden among the rope lockers on my boat, and so he had seen, as no one else had, the moment I, Leah, misjudged the tide and scraped the pier. "They'll ask me tomorrow," he said. "At the hearing. What do I say?" My stomach tightened; I had rehearsed a gentler version of that night so many times it almost felt true. But I looked at him, sixteen and soaked through, and told him to say exactly what he saw, every second of it, and that I would say the same. He nodded slowly. At Ardwick a woman boarded carrying a sleeping terrier wrapped in a scarf.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Guilt-ridden, with the narrator dwelling on her past error
Resolute, though tinged with the narrator's lingering guilt
Guilty above all, with only a passing flicker of resolve
Resentful of the boy for hiding aboard the narrator's boat
g.explanation: Leah는 사고 장면을 떠올리며 속이 조이고, 더 부드러운 거짓 설명을 연습해 왔다고 고백하며 죄책감을 드러낸다. 그러나 젖은 소년을 보고는 본 그대로 말하라고, 자신도 그렇게 하겠다고 단호하게 말한다. 죄책감이 남아 있지만 정직하겠다는 결의가 더 두드러지므로 B가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만, C는 비중을 뒤집은 어조이며, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

seed.relationship: a landlord and a long-term tenant
seed.conflict: about an object that belonged to someone gone
seed.openingStyle: 구체적인 사물이나 동작으로 시작(관사 The 로 시작하지 말 것)
seed.topicSeed: a stone bridge in Cape Town; a landlord and a long-term tenant about an object that belonged to someone gone

g.passage:
Wind tugging at their coats, NEEMA and ASTER meet midway across the old stone bridge in Cape Town. Below, the canal runs brown after rain.
ASTER: (holding out a small tin box) I found it behind the stove when I moved the shelves. I think it was your father's.
NEEMA: (opening it; inside, a pocket watch and a folded bus ticket) He kept the flat before I ever rented it to you. I thought this was lost when we cleared his things.
(She is quiet. Her thumb rests on the ticket.)
ASTER: I almost kept it another week. I didn't know how to give it back.
NEEMA: (laughing softly, eyes wet) Twenty-two years you've paid rent on time, and now you're late with this.
ASTER: Am I evicted?
NEEMA: You're forgiven.
(A cyclist rings his bell twice and swerves around them.)
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Grieving, centered on Neema's sense of her father's absence
Mournful, with only a moment of warmth between the women
Tense, marked by a dispute over the tenant's overdue rent
Warm and grateful, though touched by the ache of a loss
g.explanation: Neema는 아버지의 유품을 받고 표를 쓰다듬으며 잠시 말을 잃어 상실의 아픔을 드러낸다. 그러나 곧 눈물 젖은 채 웃으며 Aster에게 농담을 건네고 용서한다고 말해 따뜻함과 고마움이 장면을 이끈다. 따뜻함이 중심이고 슬픔은 배어 있는 정서이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만, B는 비중을 뒤집었으며, C는 농담 속 집세 언급을 실제 갈등으로 오해했다.

seed.conflict: over whether to tell the truth to a dying friend
seed.topicSeed: a printing press room in Mumbai; best friends after a move over whether to tell the truth to a dying friend

g.passage: Ink, hot metal, and the steady thud of the flatbed: I still smell and hear the press room in Mumbai whenever Sergio telephones. We set type side by side there for nine years before he moved to Goa, and he still calls me, Ishaan, his apprentice, though I outlasted him by a decade. Last week he rang about our old foreman, who is dying and keeps asking whether the shop he founded still runs. It does not; it closed in 1994. Sergio thinks we should tell him the truth. I keep picturing the foreman tapping each line of type with his thumb, proud as a father, and I am not sure what I will say. Still, I laughed when Sergio reminded me how I once printed a wedding card with the groom's name upside down. My neighbor's radio is playing an old film song through the wall.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Fondly affectionate, though unsettled by an unresolved choice
Troubled by the hard choice about what to tell the foreman
Deeply uncertain, with only a passing note of fond memory
Proud, celebrating the narrator's long career as a typesetter
g.explanation: 화자는 인쇄실의 냄새와 소리, 친구 Sergio의 농담과 거꾸로 찍힌 청첩장 일화를 떠올리며 웃는 등 애정 어린 정서를 곳곳에 드러낸다. 다만 죽어 가는 감독에게 진실을 말할지 정하지 못한 망설임이 함께 섞여 있다. 애정이 중심이고 망설임은 그 아래의 정서이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 덜 두드러진 정서만, C는 비중을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

g.passage: Bergen in July smelled of tar and wet lilac, and the long dining hall of the summer school where I worked as a boy smelled of both. I was the gardener's son, trimming hedges for Thorvald, who had bought the estate that spring. One evening he called me in while the students ate and told me, before all of them, that he would pay my fees at the cathedral school in autumn. I felt my face burn; I was holding a rake, and my boots were caked with mud. Yet when he shook my hand, his grip was so earnest that the burning turned, slowly, to something like gladness, and I thanked him twice. Jens, my father, was waiting by the kitchen door. Through the windows, gulls wheeled above the fish market.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Embarrassed, focused on the narrator's muddy appearance
Grateful, though first colored by a sense of embarrassment
Humiliated, with only a faint trace of thankfulness
Resentful of the new owner for staging a public display
g.explanation: 화자는 학생들 앞에서 장학금 소식을 듣자 진흙투성이 차림 때문에 얼굴이 달아오른다. 그러나 Thorvald의 진심 어린 악수에 그 부끄러움이 기쁨으로 바뀌고 두 번이나 감사를 표한다. 부끄러움이 먼저 있지만 감사가 더 두드러지므로 B가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만, C는 비중을 뒤집었고, D는 지문에 단서가 약한 어조다.

seed.relationship: a grandfather and a granddaughter learning his language
seed.topicSeed: a flooded cellar in Havana; a grandfather and a granddaughter learning his language over an unfinished project

g.passage: By the time you read this, Grandpa Lachlan, the water in the Havana cellar will have gone down, or so the neighbors promise. I waded in this morning to find your Gaelic word cards floating like little rafts, the ink on the S's running blue. For an hour I could only stand there and count the ruined ones. Then I remembered how you made me repeat your goodnight phrase every evening until I stopped stumbling, and I began lifting the cards out one by one and pegging them on the line across the patio. Many can still be read. I am copying each onto fresh paper, and I have learned eleven new words already, though I am sure I say half of them wrong. Your Ximena. Señora Ruiz from upstairs has lent me her fan to dry them.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Dismayed, dwelling on the ruined cards in the flooded cellar
Discouraged, with only a slight hint of determination
Determined and hopeful, after a moment of dismay
Bitter toward the neighbors for their empty promises
g.explanation: Ximena는 물에 뜬 단어 카드를 보고 한 시간 동안 망가진 것만 세며 낙담한다. 그러나 할아버지와의 기억을 떠올린 뒤 카드를 건져 말리고 새 종이에 옮기며 새 단어를 익힌다. 잠깐의 낙담 뒤 결의와 희망이 더 두드러지므로 C가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만, B는 비중을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

seed.conflict: when two traditions have to share one table
seed.openingStyle: 대명사 I 또는 We 로 시작
seed.topicSeed: a train-station cafe in Hamburg; a pair of rival bakers when two traditions have to share one table

g.passage: We had not spoken in four years, Greta and I, not since she lured my best customer across the square with her poppy-seed rolls. So when the stationmaster told us that the new café at the Hamburg terminal would have only one table for pastries, and that we must share it, I, Annika, nearly refused. On the first morning she set her rolls on the left and I set my almond cakes on the right, and neither of us looked up. By noon, though, I noticed she had moved her tray an inch to give my cakes the light from the window. Before closing, I tasted one of her rolls in the stockroom; it was better than mine, and I told her so the next day. She only sniffed and said my almonds were too dry. A train from Altona hissed to a stop beyond the glass.
g.question: Which choice best describes the relationship between Annika and Greta as presented in the text?
options: Greta resents Annika and tries to keep her from selling well at the café.
Annika admires Greta, who has come to rely on Annika's baking judgment.
They are old friends who quarrel only to amuse the café's customers.
They are rivals who are beginning to show each other a wary respect.
g.explanation: 두 사람은 4년 동안 말도 하지 않은 경쟁자였고 첫날에도 서로 쳐다보지 않는다. 그러나 Greta는 Annika의 케이크에 햇빛이 들도록 쟁반을 옮겨 주고, Annika는 Greta의 빵이 더 낫다고 인정한다. 두 장면을 이으면 경쟁 관계 속에서 조심스러운 존중이 싹트고 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 한쪽 감정만, B는 방향을 뒤집은 관계이며, C는 지문에 근거가 없는 통념이다.

seed.topicSeed: a monastery guesthouse in the Navajo plateau; an uncle and a nephew with a debt over who should stay behind

g.passage: Years later, I still remember the frost on the guesthouse windows the morning Aunt Itzel and I had to decide which of us would stay. We owed the brothers for a whole winter of lodging on the plateau, and the abbot had agreed that one of us could work it off through spring while the other drove home to Flagstaff. I, Nova, said I would stay; I was nineteen and strong, and she had a job waiting. Itzel only poured me coffee and slid the truck keys across the table toward my hand. When I pushed them back, she closed my fingers around them and said that she had stayed behind for my mother once, too, and had never regretted it. I left at noon. Snow was drifting against the mesa's red flank as I passed the cattle guard.
g.question: Which choice best describes the relationship between Itzel and Nova as presented in the text?
options: Itzel insists on sacrificing for Nova, who wants to bear the burden herself.
Nova resents Itzel for forcing her to leave the plateau guesthouse before spring.
Itzel depends on Nova, who reluctantly agrees to stay behind and work.
They are distant relatives bound together mainly by the debt they share.
g.explanation: Nova는 젊고 튼튼하다며 자신이 남겠다고 나서지만, Itzel은 말없이 트럭 열쇠를 Nova 쪽으로 밀어 준다. Nova가 열쇠를 돌려보내자 Itzel은 그녀의 손에 열쇠를 쥐여 주며 예전에도 Nova의 어머니를 위해 남았다고 말한다. 두 행동을 이으면 Itzel은 Nova를 위해 희생하려 하고 Nova는 짐을 직접 지려 하는 관계이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 한쪽 감정만, C는 방향을 뒤집은 관계이며, D는 일반적 통념에서 고른 관계다.
